terms.comment: paulum cinnamōmī is our easy way to say “a pinch of cinnamon,” without implying an exact measure. With a verb it is an adverb: paulum redormiō, I sleep a little more.
terms.grammar: noun, second declension, with a genitive (paulum silvae); with verbs, an adverb

terms.gloss: a tiny bit, a very little
terms.grammar: noun, second declension (diminutive of paulum); also an adverb
evidence: Plaut. Curc. 1.2.31: dē paulō paululum hoc tibi dabō (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: a little (with comparatives): a little more, a little earlier
terms.grammar: adverb (the ablative of the measure of difference)
terms.comment: With comparatives and with ante, post: paulō prius, a little earlier; paulō post, a little later. “Much more” is multō (see a lot).

phrases.latin: Nimis acida est? Paulum banānae addāmus.
phrases.english: Is it too sour? Let’s add a little banana.

phrases.latin: Prō peccātō magnō paulum supplicī satis est patrī.
phrases.english: For a great wrong, a little punishment is enough for a father.

phrases.latin: hoc erat in vōtīs: modus agrī nōn ita magnus, hortus ubi et tēctō vīcīnus jūgis aquae fōns et paulum silvae super hīs foret
phrases.english: this is what I prayed for: a piece of land not so very big, with a garden, a spring of running water near the house, and a bit of woodland above them
I sleep a little more, then go for a walk
but once they have gained a little strength
